title: Muhammad Ali: Float Like Greatness
description: From Olympic gold to global icon—five chapters of the Greatest.

questions.question: Which boxer promised to 'float like a butterfly, sting like a bee'?
questions.explanation: Cornerman Drew "Bundini" Brown is credited with coining it in 1964, before the Sonny Liston upset. The full chant ended: "Rumble, young man, rumble!"

questions.question: As 18-year-old Cassius Clay, Muhammad Ali won Olympic gold at which Games?
questions.explanation: Terrified of flying, he reportedly bought a parachute at an army surplus store and wore it on the plane. In the light-heavyweight final he beat Poland's Zbigniew Pietrzykowski.

questions.question: After his 1960 Rome gold, where did Ali say he tossed his Olympic medal?
questions.explanation: Wilma Rudolph remembered he never took it off in Rome: "He slept with it." His 1975 autobiography says he later flung it off a Louisville bridge in disgust.

questions.question: Ali later wrote that he threw his medal in the Ohio River—what injustice did he say drove him to it?
questions.explanation: The book says he was refused service at a whites-only Louisville restaurant, then fought a biker gang. Friends like Howard Bingham doubted the toss; Ali later admitted he'd lost it.

questions.question: Decades after the racial discrimination he said drove him to ditch it, Ali received a replacement Olympic gold in what year?
questions.explanation: Two weeks after lighting the Atlanta cauldron with trembling hands, he got a new gold from IOC chief Samaranch at halftime of the USA-Yugoslavia final. Both teams mobbed him.
